questions.prompt: What does the nervous system do in the body?
questions.explanation: The nervous system carries signals to control and coordinate all body activities.

options: Coordinates and controls all body activities

questions.prompt: What are the two main parts of the nervous system?
questions.explanation: The nervous system has the Central Nervous System (CNS) and the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS).

questions.prompt: Which two organs make up the Central Nervous System?
questions.explanation: The CNS is made up of the brain and the spinal cord.

questions.prompt: What is the basic working unit of the nervous system?
questions.explanation: A neuron (nerve cell) is the basic working unit of the nervous system.

questions.prompt: Which part of a neuron receives signals?
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive incoming signals toward the cell body.

questions.prompt: Which part of a neuron carries signals away from the cell body?
questions.explanation: The axon carries signals away from the cell body.

questions.prompt: What are the three basic parts of the human brain?
questions.explanation: The brain has three basic parts: forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest part of the human brain?
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain.

questions.prompt: What protects the brain inside the skull?
questions.explanation: The brain is protected by the hard skull and cerebrospinal fluid.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum controls balance and coordinated movements.

questions.prompt: What is the normal human body temperature?
questions.explanation: Normal body temperature is about 37°C (98.6°F).

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain acts as the body's thermostat?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus maintains body temperature like a thermostat.

questions.prompt: What is a stimulus?
questions.explanation: A stimulus is any change in the environment that the body detects and reacts to.

options: A change in the environment that causes a reaction

questions.prompt: What do receptors do?
questions.explanation: Receptors detect stimuli and send signals to the brain.

questions.prompt: What are effectors in the body?
questions.explanation: Effectors (usually muscles) produce the response to a stimulus.

questions.prompt: What does the myelin sheath do?
questions.explanation: The myelin sheath insulates the axon and speeds up nerve impulses.

options: Insulates the axon and speeds up signals

questions.prompt: A sensory neuron carries signals in which direction?
questions.explanation: Sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.

questions.prompt: A motor neuron carries signals in which direction?
questions.explanation: Motor neurons carry impulses from the CNS to muscles and glands.

options: From CNS to muscles and glands

questions.prompt: What is a synapse?
questions.explanation: A synapse is the tiny gap between two neurons where signals pass chemically.

options: The tiny gap between two neurons

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls breathing and heartbeat?
questions.explanation: The medulla controls involuntary actions like breathing and heartbeat.

questions.prompt: What is the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)?
questions.explanation: The PNS is the network of nerves connecting the CNS to receptors and effectors.

options: The network of nerves connecting CNS to the body

questions.prompt: Which three parts make up the forebrain?
questions.explanation: The forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus.

questions.prompt: Which three parts make up the hindbrain?
questions.explanation: The hindbrain consists of the cerebellum, medulla and pons.

questions.prompt: Why is the thalamus called a relay station?
questions.explanation: The thalamus relays sensory information from sense organs to the cerebrum.

options: It forwards sensory signals to the cerebrum

questions.prompt: The left cerebral hemisphere controls which side of the body?
questions.explanation: The left hemisphere controls the right side of the body.

questions.prompt: The right cerebral hemisphere controls which side of the body?
questions.explanation: The right hemisphere controls the left side of the body.

questions.prompt: Which hemisphere is mainly linked to language and logical thinking?
questions.explanation: The left hemisphere handles language, speech, maths and logic.

questions.prompt: Which hemisphere is mainly linked to creativity and art?
questions.explanation: The right hemisphere handles creativity, art, music and visual-spatial skills.

questions.prompt: Why is the midbrain called a bridge?
questions.explanation: The midbrain acts as a bridge connecting the forebrain and hindbrain.

options: It connects the forebrain and hindbrain

questions.prompt: What is peristalsis?
questions.explanation: Peristalsis is wave-like muscle contractions that push food through the digestive tract.

options: Wave-like muscle contractions that move food

questions.prompt: Why is the pituitary gland called the master gland?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland controls other glands by releasing hormones.

options: It controls other glands by releasing hormones

questions.prompt: In which direction do nerve impulses travel in a neuron?
questions.explanation: Impulses travel one way: dendrites → cell body → axon → axon terminals.

questions.prompt: What is a reflex action?
questions.explanation: A reflex action is automatic and very fast, without conscious thought.

options: An automatic, fast response without conscious thought

questions.prompt: Which structure coordinates a reflex action?
questions.explanation: The spinal cord coordinates the reflex response directly, without waiting for the brain.

questions.prompt: What carries a signal across a synapse?
questions.explanation: A neurotransmitter (chemical messenger) carries the signal across the synaptic gap.

questions.prompt: What happens when body temperature rises above normal?
questions.explanation: When too hot, the hypothalamus triggers sweating to cool the body.

questions.prompt: What happens when body temperature falls below normal?
questions.explanation: When too cold, the hypothalamus triggers shivering to produce heat.

questions.prompt: A nerve that contains both sensory and motor fibres is called a?
questions.explanation: A nerve with both sensory and motor fibres is called a mixed nerve.

questions.prompt: If the thalamus is damaged, what is most likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Thalamus damage means sensory signals are not relayed properly, causing loss of sensation and poor coordination.

options: Sensory signals are not properly relayed to the cerebrum

questions.prompt: Why does damage to the medulla threaten life immediately?
questions.explanation: The medulla controls vital involuntary functions; if it fails, breathing and heartbeat stop.

questions.prompt: If a motor nerve is damaged, what is the likely result?
questions.explanation: Motor nerve damage stops commands reaching muscles, causing paralysis.

questions.prompt: If a sensory nerve is cut, what happens in that area?
questions.explanation: A cut sensory nerve sends no signals to the brain, so that area feels nothing.

options: Loss of sensation (no pain or touch felt)

questions.prompt: Why do reflex actions happen faster than voluntary actions?
questions.explanation: In a reflex, the spinal cord responds directly without waiting for the brain, so it is faster.

options: The signal does not go to the brain first; the spinal cord acts

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of a reflex arc?
questions.explanation: The reflex arc runs: receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord (relay) → motor neuron → effector.

options: Receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector
Effector → motor neuron → spinal cord → receptor

questions.prompt: Why do we still feel pain shortly after a reflex pulls our hand away?
questions.explanation: The spinal cord handles the reflex first; a signal reaches the brain a moment later, so we feel pain after.

options: A signal also reaches the brain after the reflex

questions.prompt: Why does chemical transmission at a synapse ensure one-way signalling?
questions.explanation: Chemicals are released by the axon terminal and received by the next neuron's dendrites, so signals go one way.

options: Neurotransmitters are released on one side and received on the other

questions.prompt: Why does a wrinkled (folded) brain surface make the brain more powerful?
questions.explanation: Folds increase the surface area, letting more neurons fit inside the skull.

options: Folds increase surface area so more neurons fit

questions.prompt: Why can a person ride a bicycle automatically after learning?
questions.explanation: After practice, the cerebellum stores the movement pattern and runs it automatically.

options: The cerebellum stores the learned movement pattern

questions.prompt: Why does the pupil get smaller in bright light?
questions.explanation: The pupil reflex is automatic and limits light entering to protect the sensitive retina.

options: A reflex protects the retina by limiting light

questions.prompt: What best explains why involuntary actions like breathing continue during sleep?
questions.explanation: The medulla runs involuntary actions automatically, so they continue even during sleep.

options: The medulla controls them automatically, no thought needed
